issues.description: CloseStream message uses wrong type value 'Close' instead of 'CloseStream'
issues.detail: The PR description and Deepgram's API specify the control message must be {"type": "CloseStream"}, but the code sets _CLOSE_MSG = json.dumps({"type": "Close"}). This sends an invalid/unrecognized message, defeating the purpose of the fix. Deepgram will likely ignore it and audio truncation will persist.

issues.description: send_str on an already-closed or closing WebSocket will raise and may mask the real error
issues.detail: If _close_ws is called after the connection is already half-closed (network error, server-initiated close), send_str raises ConnectionResetError/ClientError. The broad except catches it and logs a warning, but the original failure context is lost. Consider checking ws.closed before sending.

issues.description: Single receive() call may consume a data frame instead of waiting for close acknowledgment
issues.detail: ws.receive() returns the next message of any type — could be a buffered audio chunk rather than the server's close frame. This discards potentially useful final audio (the very thing the fix is meant to preserve) and does not actually confirm graceful shutdown. A loop draining until WSMsgType.CLOSE would be more correct.

issues.description: Hardcoded 1.0s timeout has no configuration knob
issues.detail: The 1-second wait for server acknowledgment is hardcoded. On slow networks or large pending audio buffers this may be too short; on fast paths it adds latency to every disconnect. Consider exposing via conn_options or making it a module constant for tuning.

issues.description: f-string used in logger.warning instead of lazy %-formatting
issues.detail: logger.warning(f"Error during WebSocket close sequence: {e}") eagerly formats the string even when the log level filters it out. Prefer logger.warning("Error during WebSocket close sequence: %s", e) for consistency with logging best practices and to capture exc_info for debugging.

review.summary: The fix has the right intent but contains a likely correctness bug: the close control message is serialized as {"type": "Close"} rather than {"type": "CloseStream"} per Deepgram's documented API and this PR's own description. Secondary concerns: the single receive() call may consume a useful audio frame instead of the close ack, send_str on an already-closed socket will land in the broad except and silently swallow errors, and the 1s timeout is hardcoded. Verify the exact message Deepgram's Speak v1 socket expects before merging.
